title: Authoritative managed path survey
objective: Establish one fail-closed managed-path survey and make every checkpoint consumer respect its registry-aware safety result.

phases.title: Safe discovery primitives
phases.objective: Represent path safety explicitly before any managed artifact is read or enumerated.

tasks.title: Harden managed path validation
tasks.description: Make assertSafeManagedPath detect dangling symlinks and reject symlinked or non-directory ancestors without following them.
tasks.context: existsSync treats a dangling symlink as absent, so the current component walk can skip it.
acceptance_criteria: Every existing path component is inspected with lstat semantics.
Dangling symlinks and non-directory intermediate components are rejected.
Lexical and real-path workspace escape protections remain intact.

evidence.summary: Hardened managed-path ancestry checks and stabilized lease-worker startup under filesystem load.

checked_criteria: Every existing path component is inspected with lstat semantics.

tasks.title: Make checkpoint survey authoritative
tasks.description: Extend the survey with container status, issue level and safe entry facts; never collapse unsafe or unreadable paths to an empty survey.
tasks.context: The current survey catches an unsafe archive ancestor and returns an empty list while ownership discovery performs a separate unsafe enumeration.
acceptance_criteria: Scope root, sprint, archive and checkpoint safety are observable without dereferencing links.
Only safe regular candidates reach checkpoint resolution.
Ownership scanning never enumerates an unsafe archive or record directory.
The five directory classes remain unchanged and path issues remain a separate axis.

evidence.summary: Implemented the canonical checkpoint survey with explicit root, sprint, archive and checkpoint safety facts.

checked_criteria: Scope root, sprint, archive and checkpoint safety are observable without dereferencing links.

phases.title: Registry-aware consumer parity
phases.objective: Apply the same safety facts to classification, repair, Doctor and checkpoint consumers.

tasks.title: Apply the registry and evidence matrix
tasks.description: Keep unregistered unsafe entries without Kyro evidence foreign and advisory, while treating registered or evidenced unsafe state as owned-damaged; protect rehydrate and unregister.
tasks.context: A registered unsafe directory is owned state, but an arbitrary unregistered symlink must not become a global blocker.
acceptance_criteria: Foreign unsafe entries are never registered and warn only globally.
Registered unsafe entries are owned-damaged and never unregister targets.
Safe foreign contamination remains cleanable.
Apply diverges if a prepared foreign directory becomes unsafe or owned.

evidence.summary: Applied the registry-by-evidence matrix to reconciliation, rehydration, resolution and unregister apply.

checked_criteria: Foreign unsafe entries are never registered and warn only globally.
Registered unsafe entries are owned-damaged and never unregister targets.
Safe foreign contamination remains cleanable.
Apply diverges if a prepared foreign directory becomes unsafe or owned.

tasks.title: Unify Integrity and Doctor
tasks.description: Render the survey's issues consistently and exclude every unsafe path from operations, commitments, canonicalization, latest-checkpoint selection, retirement and resume.
tasks.context: A valid registered scope with a symlinked archive currently produces a clean Integrity plan and a failing Doctor result.
acceptance_criteria: Integrity and Doctor identify the same unsafe managed path.
Unsafe paths create no operations or before-commitments.
Only safeFiles feed latest-checkpoint, canonicalization and resume.
Duplicate findings for one issue are suppressed.

evidence.summary: Unified Integrity, Doctor, close-sprint, remediation and retirement around safe checkpoint inputs.

checked_criteria: Integrity and Doctor identify the same unsafe managed path.

phases.title: Adversarial certification
phases.objective: Prove isolation, no-dereference, cleanup compatibility and load-bearing guards.

tasks.title: Extend the blast-radius matrix
tasks.description: Add portable root, sprint, archive, record and checkpoint path fixtures plus target-mutation and prepare/apply divergence coverage to the existing gate.
tasks.context: The current gate covers direct checkpoint links but does not make the candidate type or ancestor-path guard independently load-bearing.
acceptance_criteria: All ten scenarios execute in real CLI sandboxes.
Target contents behind a symlink cannot change results.
Type, path, container and catch-to-empty mutations each break the intended assertion.
No new check script is added.

evidence.summary: Extended existing gates with adversarial managed-path, no-dereference, rehydrate and prepare/apply race coverage.

acceptance_criteria: Documentation matches the implemented matrix.

tasks.title: Run full certification
tasks.description: Execute package, real-workspace, adversarial and independent QA gates and record only evidence produced by the actual commands.
tasks.context: A green suite without the ancestor-link reproduction is insufficient certification.
acceptance_criteria: Typecheck, build, full check, diff-check and pack dry-run pass.
Global Integrity and all relevant scoped Doctors pass on the real workspace.
Prepare, Doctor and close-sprint agree in the adversarial retry.

definitionOfDone: No managed discovery read follows a symlink at any relevant level.
Integrity and Doctor agree for every safe, foreign, damaged and recoverable fixture.
Foreign unsafe debris cannot block unrelated scopes or influence classification through its target.
Registered or independently owned unsafe state never produces a write operation or recovery promise.
Safe registry contamination remains cleanable and unsafe divergence aborts without writes.
Every requested gate and mutation falsification passes for the intended reason.
